text: Samsung forecasts Q3 operating profit of 107.4 trillion won (+782% YoY) and revenue of 195 trillion won (+127% YoY). AI memory demand remains elevated amid tight supply and multiyear purchasing agreements. Shares decline following the preliminary release.

meta.note: Figures are preliminary; divisional earnings remain undisclosed.

text: The NFL files a Supreme Court amicus brief supporting New Jersey regulators against Kalshi. Federal appeals courts remain divided over state gambling jurisdiction and CFTC oversight of sports prediction contracts. The NFL supports state regulation and restrictions on contract categories and participant age.

meta.note: Jurisdiction remains unresolved; league preferences are recorded as formal positions, not operative rules.

text: Skydance completes its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, combining studios, television networks, streaming platforms, and over 200 million subscribers. The entity carries roughly $80 billion in debt, unified ad sales, and separate CBS and CNN editorial operations.

meta.note: Streaming integration and cost reductions remain planned; editorial separation is an established governance condition.

text: Amazon introduces Alexa tablets priced from $230 to $550 and ends new Fire tablet production. The devices use standard Android instead of Fire OS, integrate Alexa AI features, and retain access to Amazon services. Existing Fire devices remain supported for four years after final shipment.

meta.note: Fire support continues during the product transition; memory-cost attribution remains disputed.

text: Trump states that U.S. attacks on Iran will not occur before the Nov. 3 midterms. The U.S. naval blockade remains active, additional forces are deploying to the region, and discussions with Tehran are reported as ongoing.

meta.note: The restriction is a presidential declaration, not a verified operational order; post-election action remains unspecified.

text: SpaceX agrees to acquire up to 14 MHz of paired 800 MHz spectrum from Grain Management, pending FCC approval. The portfolio spans nationwide mobile frequencies. AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile shares decline in extended trading.

meta.note: Spectrum transfer remains conditional on FCC approval; network deployment and service availability are unspecified.
